Some phones block automatic startup. If OpenXPlay Relay does not open, open it manually.

CarPlay offers Siri and calls only when microphone permission is allowed. With Head unit selected, microphone audio comes from the head unit. Notifications show the running session. Wireless CarPlay uses Bluetooth and nearby Wi-Fi devices; older Android versions require precise location for Wi-Fi discovery. Android 17 also requires local-network access for USB and wireless. USB requires Android VPN consent to route the iPhone network. Only permissions needed by the selected mode and existing location-reporting setting are requested. If a permission was permanently denied, use Open Android app permissions to allow it.
Allow Android VPN access for the USB connection.
CarPlay head-unit display. Use the web receiver for touch controls.

Enter the current six-digit PIN shown on the head unit. It rotates every 120 seconds.

Use the same name and password as in Android\'s hotspot settings.

Use the 5 GHz band: change it in Android\'s hotspot settings, because the picture often stutters on 2.4 GHz. If the head unit cannot join a 5 GHz hotspot, switch back to 2.4 GHz. Some phones offer only 2.4 GHz while connected to Wi-Fi; disconnect Wi-Fi first.

Wireless is recommended. A USB cable often causes two problems:
This phone powers the iPhone through the cable. Its battery drains fast and it may get warm, and it usually can’t charge while the cable is in.

With a USB-C to USB-C cable, the iPhone often takes control and this phone can’t see it. Use a USB-C OTG adapter on this phone with a USB-A to USB-C cable, or a USB-C to Lightning cable for a Lightning iPhone. Charge-only cables don’t work, and a loose plug drops CarPlay while you drive.
The iPhone connects straight to this phone. The car screen uses this phone\'s normal Wi-Fi, for example the car\'s hotspot.
Turn on this phone\'s hotspot. The iPhone and the car screen both join it.
The iPhone, this phone and the car screen join the same Wi-Fi, such as the car\'s hotspot or a travel router.

Reconnect when the window size changes

After the car changes the Carlink area (for example from two thirds of the screen to full screen), the first touch reconnects Carlink to fit the new size. The picture stops for a few seconds while it reconnects.

Automatic display mode only. Uses the whole-screen canvas and disables automatic CarPlay re-fit restarts. Areas apply at the next connection; reconnect manually. The relay switches areas to match the visible window, and the page shows only the active area. Switch results mean queued, not confirmed by the iPhone.

If your model year has no built-in screen data, copy these data and send them to the developers in the group. A future version can include them, giving owners of the same car a better-fitting CarPlay experience.

Declares this width to the iPhone instead of the selected screen width, to find where iOS changes the CarPlay layout. Applies at the next CarPlay start.

The web service could not start. Retrying automatically.
This phone is not on a network the head unit can reach. Join the head unit’s hotspot or Wi-Fi, or turn on this phone’s hotspot.
Automatic uses H.265 when the head unit’s browser can decode it in hardware and falls back to H.264 if it fails. The forced choices are for testing.
Automatic sends H.265 to head units that advertise support; Off always sends H.264. Reconnect Carlink after changing.
Shows frame rate, resolution, bit rate and dropped frames on the running page. Values appear once the chosen period has been measured. Off measures nothing.
CarPlay audio over the car\'s Bluetooth (experimental)

The relay offers the iPhone no CarPlay audio, so music, navigation and calls play over the iPhone\'s own Bluetooth connection with the car. Keep the iPhone paired with the car and choose Bluetooth as the car\'s audio source. If the sound plays on the iPhone instead, turn this off.
Open the head-unit page without a certificate warning, using a free domain name.
Each provider keeps its own name and token. Switching shows what is saved for it.

Sign in at duckdns.org (from mainland China, use a GitHub account), add a name, then copy the token at the top of the page. Enter the full name, such as myrelay.duckdns.org. This token can change every name in the account, so keep it like a password.

Sign up at dynv6.com with an email address, create a zone ending in .dynv6.net, then create an HTTP token on the Keys page, limited to this zone if you can. Enter the full name, such as myrelay.dynv6.net.
Copy it from your provider account. It stays on this relay.

Remove every provider’s name and token, and the certificate, from this relay? The address records at the providers stay.

Car window: CarPlay is sized to the Carlink window. 1280×720, corrected: for head units that only accept 1280×720; the picture is pre-stretched so it shows in the right shape. Reconnect Carlink after changing.
Turn on this phone’s hotspot before you start.
This phone’s hotspot is off. Turn on the hotspot, then start again.

This phone is connected over USB as a device, so it cannot see the iPhone. The other end (an iPhone, computer or car port) is acting as the host. A USB-C iPhone on a USB-C to USB-C cable usually takes control. Use a USB-C OTG adapter (USB-C to USB-A) on this phone, then a USB-A to USB-C cable to the iPhone. If this phone has an OTG switch, turn it on, then unplug and plug in again. For a Lightning iPhone, use a USB-C to Lightning cable.
Tesla’s browser does not open local-network addresses, so the relay page needs another address. This phone adds one through a local VPN (by default 169.254.88.1); nothing leaves the phone.

Needs Trusted HTTPS. Your trusted name points to %1$s on this phone, so the Tesla opens https://your-name:8443 without a certificate warning. The Tesla needs internet through this phone’s hotspot to look up the name.
No account needed. Open https://%1$s:8443 in the Tesla and continue past the certificate warning. This works only if the Tesla browser lets you continue.
Enter an IPv4 address outside 10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x and the other reserved ranges.
Android 13 and later may drop connections from the hotspot to this address (seen on Android 15). If the Tesla cannot open the page, use a 169.254 address.
Connect the Tesla to this phone’s hotspot (5 GHz if possible) or its Wi-Fi Direct network, and turn on Remain Connected in Drive in the Tesla’s Wi-Fi settings. Needs MCU2 or later.
A Tesla shows CarPlay in its browser: choose Car browser in Settings → Output.
Tesla adaptation needs wireless CarPlay: the USB connection already uses Android’s only VPN.
Tesla adaptation needs this phone’s hotspot or Wi-Fi Direct. A shared Wi-Fi router does not pass the address to this phone.

Allow this permission so CarPlay can stay on the car display while the relay is in the background.
Miracast and Carlink both use Wi-Fi Direct. Most phones can use only one at a time.
Miracast can replace CarPlay’s Wi-Fi Direct group, so use the local hotspot or USB.
Switch CarPlay to the local hotspot because Miracast can replace its Wi-Fi Direct group?
Start screen casting to the car

Miracast uses the size negotiated with the car. DLNA uses the car screen saved from the browser or the chosen car model, otherwise 16:9. The 720p/1080p size class applies to DLNA.
Ignore the car’s reported size and choose the picture proportions yourself. Use even numbers: landscape 640–1920 × 360–1080 pixels, with the bounds reversed for portrait.
A connected interactive output, such as the car browser, takes priority when choosing the CarPlay canvas. A fixed size in Car screen settings overrides every output’s size.
CarPlay uses the fixed size from Car screen settings.
Turn on if the car stretches the picture to its screen; the relay then stretches CarPlay to the whole cast picture so the car shows it in the right proportions.
Controls all experimental options below and keeps your choices when off. Changes take effect on the next connection indicated by each option; a running session stays connected.
For finding out why a paired car connects only while it shows the six-digit code. Changes apply to the next Carlink connection.
Skips the 2-second subscription wait on cars that never answer it, such as the Xpeng G6.
While Carlink is on and not connected, scan without pauses instead of 8-second scans with growing waits.

Writes every nearby Bluetooth advertisement to the Carlink debug log while scanning. Needs Carlink debug on and this phone\'s screen on. Other people\'s nearby devices are recorded too, and exported logs include them.

Sends the address you enter to the car instead of the generated one. Find it on the phone\'s About phone or Status page. Pair this phone with the car in Bluetooth settings to test whether the car then reconnects by itself.
Enter a valid Bluetooth address: XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX.
Affects wireless CarPlay input for browser and Carlink outputs.
Affects the Carlink connection to the head unit.

Keep the head-unit network specific to Carlink, reducing interference with the iPhone connection. With both outputs enabled, this also changes network selection for browser connections. Takes effect on the next Carlink connection.
Wait for Carlink before connecting the iPhone

For wireless CarPlay with Carlink output. Wait up to one minute for the head unit to be ready, then connect the iPhone. With both outputs enabled, this also delays the browser picture. Takes effect on the next CarPlay start.
Check and recover the iPhone Wi-Fi connection

Try this when Wi-Fi connects but CarPlay does not start. Check for network changes and retry an incomplete wireless session while keeping the output connection. Applies to browser and Carlink outputs on the next CarPlay connection.
Beta releases arrive before stable releases to test new features and may be less reliable. Checking for updates connects to GitHub.
